title: Rhodes stitch geometric panel
subtitle: A framed panel of interlocking Rhodes stitch squares with a basketweave background on 13-count canvas
excerpt: Rhodes stitch creates raised, three-dimensional squares from layered spoke stitches. This small framed panel arranges nine Rhodes stitch squares in a three-by-three grid against a basketweave background. Finished size is 18 by 18 cm.
sourceNotes: Rhodes stitch construction from Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), raised canvas stitch chapter. Grid arrangement synthesised from geometric stitch patterns in Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882).

glossaryTerms.definition: A needlepoint stitch that builds up above the canvas surface in multiple layers. Rhodes stitch and velvet stitch are the two most common raised stitches in traditional canvaswork.

heroPrompt: A small square framed needlepoint panel showing a three-by-three grid of raised Rhodes stitch squares in deep red on cream, showing the three-dimensional texture, natural side light.

content.text: that stands noticeably above the canvas surface. Each square uses 8 to 16 spoke stitches radiating from the corners of a square, layered in sequence. This panel places nine Rhodes stitch squares in a 3 by 3 grid on a basketweave background, with a narrow plain border. The design area is 94 by 94 holes, finishing at 18 by 18 cm.

items.label: Canvas
items.value: 13-count mono canvas, cut 29 by 29 cm (leaves a 5 cm margin around the 94 by 94 hole design area)

items.label: Thread: Rhodes squares
items.value: Persian wool. Suggested: DMC 816 / Anchor 1005 (garnet). About 20 m. Each Rhodes stitch square at 6 by 6 holes uses about 1.5 m

items.label: Thread: background
items.value: Persian wool. Suggested: DMC 712 / Anchor 926 (cream). About 15 m

items.label: Thread: border
items.value: Persian wool. Suggested: DMC 838 / Anchor 1088 (very dark beige brown). About 4 m

content.text: Border: DMC 838 / Anchor 1088: very dark beige brown
Mount on a frame. The Rhodes stitch spokes pull the canvas at multiple angles; a frame keeps the background fill stable around the raised squares.
: 8 spoke stitches over a 6 by 6 hole square, each spoke from a corner to the opposite corner, worked in strict sequence

Mark the design boundary and the 3 by 3 grid of Rhodes stitch positions. Each Rhodes square occupies a 6 by 6 hole area; the nine squares are spaced 4 holes apart with the border running 8 holes in from the canvas edge.

Work all nine Rhodes stitch squares first. Work each square from the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner in the first spoke, rotating clockwise for each subsequent spoke. The layered spokes build up the raised centre automatically as each row is completed.
Work the border in the dark shade using basketweave tent stitch.
Fill the cream background in basketweave, working carefully around the base of each Rhodes stitch square.
Block the finished canvas by dampening and pressing under a book for a few hours. Full pin-blocking would flatten the raised Rhodes stitches; pressing only is correct here.
Lace the blocked canvas over the acid-free board and fit into a square picture frame. A narrow frame in a contrasting colour suits the geometric character of the design.
A 5 by 5 grid of Rhodes stitch squares at a smaller 4 by 4 hole scale, on 18-count canvas, gives the same raised texture in a finer, more delicate scale.
